react_result.final_narrative_text: Multi-paradigm enrichment of eight differentially abundant metabolites reveals a convergent picture of disrupted biological oxidation and phase-I xenobiotic metabolism. RaMP multi-database ORA ranked REACT:R-HSA-211859 "Biological oxidations" as the top hit (FDR = 1.33e-4, fold enrichment = 124), driven by methimazole, coumarin, and L-cysteine. The same three compounds appear in the Reactome Phase I functionalization pathway (FDR = 2.19e-3), consistent with cytochrome-P450-mediated compound transformation. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently validated cysteine-centred pathways: hsa00730 Thiamine metabolism, hsa00430 Cysteine metabolism, hsa00480 Glutathione metabolism, and hsa00670 One carbon pool by folate, all anchored on L-cysteine as the sole hit (p < 0.05). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returned "Xenobiotics metabolism" (MUMM pathway, p = 0.0045) as the top network hit, with coumarin as the primary mapped compound. The cross-paradigm consensus is therefore: a diverse set of xenobiotic compounds — coumarin, benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide I, N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl, and pyrocatechol (catechol) — co-occurs with altered cysteine/glutathione metabolism in the treatment group, consistent with induced oxidative stress and phase-I detoxication enzyme activity. L-Cysteine is the central driver: it participates in glutathione biosynthesis, iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis (WP:WP4487), and serves as a nucleophile that conjugates electrophilic xenobiotic intermediates. Bromide (CHEBI:15858) is a likely bystander from halogenated compound exposure and does not independently drive any enriched pathway. The convergence of ORA, m/z-network, and KEGG PSEA on xenobiotic-handling pathways with cysteine as the hub metabolite constitutes strong multi-method evidence for treatment-induced disruption of phase-I/II detoxication metabolism.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms were applied to the eight differentially abundant metabolites. RaMP multi-database ORA returned Biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859) as the top hit (FDR = 0.0019, raw p = 1.09 × 10⁻⁴), with L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097, InChIKey: XUJNEKJLAYXESH) and coumarin (KEGG:C05851, InChIKey: ZYGHJZDHTFUPRJ) as the two intersecting member metabolites across a 327-member pathway. Mummichog network-based analysis independently returned Xenobiotics metabolism (MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism) ranked first (p = 0.0053), also implicating coumarin alongside an empirical network counterpart. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed L-cysteine as the sole driver across four additional KEGG pathways (hsa00730, hsa00430, hsa00770, hsa00670), all with L-cysteine as the single input-hit. The convergence across ORA (RaMP), network-based (mummichog), and KEGG-specific PSEA (MetaboAnalystR) on L-cysteine and coumarin as signal drivers identifies cysteine-associated biological oxidations and xenobiotic-phase metabolism as the primary affected biological processes. The remaining six input metabolites did not reach annotation coverage in the background sets of any paradigm.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms were applied to the eight differentially abundant metabolites. RaMP multi-database ORA returned Biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859) as the top hit (FDR = 0.0019, raw p = 1.09 × 10⁻⁴), with L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097, InChIKey: XUJNEKJLAYXESH) and coumarin (KEGG:C05851, InChIKey: ZYGHJZDHTFUPRJ) as the two intersecting member metabolites across a 327-member pathway. Mummichog network-based analysis independently returned Xenobiotics metabolism (MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism) ranked first (p = 0.0053), also implicating coumarin alongside an empirical network counterpart. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed L-cysteine as the sole driver across four additional KEGG pathways (hsa00730, hsa00430, hsa00770, hsa00670), all with L-cysteine as the single input-hit. The convergence across ORA (RaMP), network-based (mummichog), and KEGG-specific PSEA (MetaboAnalystR) on L-cysteine and coumarin as signal drivers identifies cysteine-associated biological oxidations and xenobiotic-phase metabolism as the primary affected biological processes. The remaining six input metabolites did not reach annotation coverage in the background sets of any paradigm.
